patch.value: Omission receipts: every bounded read shape names the field groups it withheld and the flag that restores each, with the same rigor row truncation already has

Bounded reads tell a caller what they contain and never what they withheld, so an agent cannot decide whether paying more would answer its question. Row omission already has a full receipt: a count, a has_more, an applied bound and a resumable cursor. Field and section omission has no receipt at all on most surfaces and five different partial ones across the rest. Measured 2026-07-29.

The five answers to one question. pm list emits a projection object naming its mode and the exact field list it produced. pm context emits sections_included and names the sections honestly, empty at brief, six names at standard, ten at deep. pm activity emits only a boolean named compact and no field list. pm search emits no projection key of any kind. pm get emits nothing at all outside the item at brief depth, silently dropping children, claim_state and linked, all three of which appear at standard.

The polarity is wrong even where a receipt exists. Every declaration names what is present. A caller deciding whether to spend more tokens needs the complement, and computing the complement requires already knowing the full field set for that command, which is the knowledge the caller was trying to avoid loading. The receipt has to name the omission directly and name the flag that restores it, the same way the row receipt names has_more and hands back a cursor rather than expecting the caller to derive one.

Why this matters more than it sounds. In every measured pair the expensive shape is the only one carrying the answer. activity --full is the only projection that carries agent provenance, and it costs 63.5 times the compact shape. contracts --full is the only complete declared surface, and it costs 96 times the default. health plain is the only shape with extension detail. The cheap default is cheap because it dropped what was asked for, and today it drops it silently, so the failure mode is an agent that reads a complete-looking payload, concludes the data is absent, and files a wrong finding. That has already happened in this tracker more than once, and the recorded traps about wrong jq keys and empty decoy arrays are the same failure wearing a different hat.

Scope. This item adds the receipt; it does not change what any shape emits by default. No payload gets larger except by the size of the receipt itself, which is bounded by the number of declared field groups per command and is therefore small and constant. Choosing the default shape stays with the parent budget contract. Which key names the projection, and that every read surface has one, stays with pm-sb0tns. Envelopes that report a count beside an empty array stay with pm-cyrfjq, which is the failure this receipt would have made visible.

value.text: Duplicate check before create: pm-oi4zs3 is CLOSED and made lean reads OMIT caller echoes, which is the opposite operation to declaring an omission; pm-cyrfjq owns envelopes that report a count beside an empty array, a defect this receipt would expose rather than a receipt; pm-pjnu91 owns the three incompatible list-family projections, which is about which fields are chosen and not about disclosing the choice; pm-sb0tns owns the row contract and the --fields axis. Searched keyword and semantic for omission receipt, projection declaration, withheld fields; inspected the live envelopes of list, context, activity, search and get to confirm five distinct behaviours.

author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: Every read command that supports more than one output shape emits an omission receipt naming the withheld field groups or sections, and for each one the exact flag that restores it; A shape that withholds nothing emits an explicit empty receipt, so a complete payload and a missing receipt can never look alike; The receipt is derived from the same declared contract that drives the shapes, so adding a field group makes it appear in the receipt with no per-command edit, proven by a fixture group no command declares today; The receipt is bounded and constant per command: a test asserts its size does not scale with the number of rows or the size of the corpus; pm get at brief depth names children, claim_state and linked as withheld, and pm activity in compact mode names the provenance group as withheld, because both are silent today and both are the cases that produced wrong conclusions; Row omission and field omission use one vocabulary: the receipt keys read consistently against the existing has_more, applied_limit and next_cursor keys rather than introducing a parallel naming scheme

message: Acceptance criteria for contract-derived, bounded, explicit omission receipts
